subject: Ownership deconflict, checkpoints, and acceptance criteria for AtlasHealth MAP
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Avery Collins <avery.collins@atlashealth.com>; Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ownership deconflict, checkpoints, and acceptance criteria for AtlasHealth MAP

Hi Avery / Rajesh —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. As discussed, I wanted to capture a concise mutual action plan (MAP) skeleton so we can lock owners, hard checkpoints, and acceptance criteria for the pilot. I attached a first-pass spreadsheet (Atlas-MAP-v1.xlsx) with milestone rows and proposed dates.

Key asks from our side:
- Confirm the go/no-go acceptance criteria for the pilot (security, latency, success metrics).
- Identify the Atlas owners for each milestone (integration, test data, security review).
- Call out any blackout windows or procurement gating items that would shift the timeline.

Proposed high level timeline (subject to your confirmation):
1) Integration kickoff — 2025-11-03 (owner: Atlas eng)
2) Data ingestion & test set delivery — 2025-11-17 (owner: Atlas product)
3) Internal end-to-end dry run — 2025-11-28 (owner: Redwood eng)
4) Pilot go-live (soft) — 2025-12-08 (combined acceptance)

Please reply with ownership updates and any must-have shifts by EOD Friday so we can finalize and start resourcing. If it's helpful, I can host a 30-min alignment session tomorrow.

Thanks —
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com] | (415) 555-0132

From: Avery Collins <avery.collins@atlashealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <rajesh.patel@atlashealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 11:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Ownership deconflict, checkpoints, and acceptance criteria for AtlasHealth MAP

Jordan —

Thanks for the note and the workbook. Quick responses inline: 

- Integration kickoff: we can commit to 2025-11-03 but need a detailed integration checklist from Marcus' team (API schema, auth, sample payloads).
- Test data: we will deliver a labeled subset on 2025-11-19 (two days later than proposed) — Rajesh will own this.
- Dry run: Nov 30 seems safer for us given our change freeze Nov 25–27.
- Pilot soft go-live: Dec 10 preferred (we have a weekend maintenance window Dec 5–6 that may impact the finalization).

Acceptance criteria (Atlas):
1) SOC2 evidence for logging retention (we need confirmation of log export cadence).
2) 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for 512-token prompts under pilot load.
3) No PII leakage observed in 3 sample prompt suites.

Risks: our procurement has an outstanding vendor questionnaire that needs legal sign-off — target completion 2025-11-12. If that slips, we may need to push the kick.

I'll be OOO Thursday afternoon but Rajesh will coordinate.

—Avery
Avery Collins
VP Product, Atlas Health
avery.collins@atlashealth.com | +1 312-555-0199
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ownership deconflict, checkpoints, and acceptance criteria for AtlasHealth MAP

Thanks for the clear responses, Avery. Two operational notes from CS side: 

1) Acceptance gate: in addition to Atlas' three items, Redwood requires a test harness run with the production-like traffic profile (we usually run a 2-hour soak at 50qps). We propose scheduling that for the dry run window.
2) Owner matrix: Jordan and I will be primary exec escalation contacts; we need Atlas' single technical owner for day-to-day issues (Rajesh is fine). Please add a primary phone contact for on-call windows.

I updated the attached workbook with the shifted dates and the soak requirement.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Success Director | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 16 Oct 2025 14:20:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Ownership deconflict, checkpoints, and acceptance criteria for AtlasHealth MAP

Dropping in from engineering — quick technical clarifications and requests: 

- Integration checklist: I'll send the API contract and auth flow by EOD tomorrow. We need Atlas to confirm OAuth client provisioning lead time (typically 3–5 business days).
- Data ingestion: to keep the pilot isolated, we recommend using the sandbox bucket pattern; Atlas must provide IAM role or presigned uploads by 11/19.
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 350ms is achievable on our Dedicated pilot size, but we will need the exact token distribution for the sample prompts. Can Atlas share token histograms?

Potential blockers: if procurement requires an on-prem data path, that adds ~4 weeks to lead time. Otherwise, planned schedule looks tight but doable.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick alignment, everyone — summarizing next steps and owners so we have a single source of truth: 

Milestones & owners (final):
- Integration kickoff (2025-11-03) — Atlas eng owner: Rajesh Patel; Redwood eng lead: Marcus Lin
- Test data delivery (2025-11-19) — Atlas product owner: Avery Collins / Rajesh Patel
- Post-delivery validation & soak (2025-11-30) — Redwood eng ops lead: Marcus Lin; CS acceptance: Naomi Feldman
- Soft pilot go-live (2025-12-10) — Joint acceptance (Atlas + Redwood)

Action items:
- Marcus: API contract + auth guide by 2025-10-18 (integration-deps-IDS-2025.pdf attached).
- Rajesh: confirm OAuth provisioning timeline & provide token histogram by 2025-10-22.
- Avery: expedite procurement questionnaire; target legal sign-off by 2025-11-12.
- Naomi/Jordan: schedule weekly 30-min checkpoints starting week of 2025-10-20; first session Tues 10/21.

I'll upload the updated MAP workbook and a one-page acceptance checklist to the shared Drive after this note. If anything here is off, call it out now — otherwise we'll treat this as the agreed baseline and circulate the DOC link.

Thanks —
Jordan
